ssri.name: SSRIs (Antidepressants)

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Supports mood alongside SSRIs. Studies show EPA-dominant fish oil enhances antidepressant response and reduces residual symptoms.

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: SSRIs can deplete magnesium. Supplementing supports relaxation, sleep quality, and may reduce SSRI-related anxiety and muscle tension.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: SSRIs deplete folate and B6. Methylated B vitamins support neurotransmitter production and enhance antidepressant efficacy.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Low vitamin D is linked to depression severity. Supplementing supports mood regulation without interfering with SSRIs.

safe.name: Zinc
safe.reason: SSRIs deplete zinc. Zinc plays a key role in serotonin synthesis and supplementing may improve antidepressant response.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: The gut-brain axis influences mood. Probiotics support serotonin production (90% made in the gut) and reduce GI side effects of SSRIs.

safe.name: Vitamin C
safe.reason: Antioxidant support that may be depleted by SSRIs. Helps with dopamine and norepinephrine synthesis.

caution.name: SAMe
caution.reason: SAMe raises serotonin and may enhance SSRIs but carries a low risk of serotonin syndrome. Use only under medical supervision.

caution.name: Melatonin
caution.reason: Generally safe at low doses (0.5-3 mg) but SSRIs like fluvoxamine can increase melatonin levels. Start low and monitor.

caution.name: Curcumin
caution.reason: Has mild serotonergic activity. Likely safe at standard doses but discuss with your doctor if taking high-dose extracts.

avoid.name: St. John's Wort
avoid.reason: Strongly increases serotonin activity. Combining with SSRIs creates serious risk of serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening condition.

avoid.name: 5-HTP
avoid.reason: Directly increases serotonin production. Combined with SSRIs, this can cause serotonin syndrome with symptoms including agitation, rapid heart rate, and hyperthermia.

avoid.name: L-Tryptophan
avoid.reason: A serotonin precursor that raises serotonin levels. Combining with SSRIs significantly increases serotonin syndrome risk.

ssri.timing_note: Take supplements with meals for consistent absorption. Maintain a regular schedule alongside your SSRI.

metformin.name: Metformin (Diabetes)

safe.name: Vitamin B12
safe.reason: Metformin depletes B12 in up to 30% of long-term users. Supplementing restores levels and prevents peripheral neuropathy and cognitive decline.

safe.name: Folate
safe.reason: Metformin impairs folate absorption. Methylfolate supplementation supports homocysteine metabolism and cardiovascular health.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Diabetic patients are often vitamin D deficient. D3 supports insulin sensitivity and bone health without affecting blood sugar control.

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: Diabetes increases magnesium excretion. Supplementing improves insulin sensitivity and glycemic control synergistically with metformin.

safe.name: Chromium
safe.reason: Chromium picolinate enhances insulin receptor sensitivity. Works synergistically with metformin to improve glucose uptake.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Reduces cardiovascular risk, which is elevated in diabetic patients. Does not significantly affect blood glucose control.

safe.name: Alpha-Lipoic Acid
safe.reason: Improves insulin sensitivity and protects against diabetic neuropathy. Complements metformin's mechanism of action.

safe.name: CoQ10
safe.reason: Metformin may reduce CoQ10 levels. Supplementing supports mitochondrial energy production and cardiovascular health.

caution.name: Berberine
caution.reason: Has metformin-like blood sugar lowering effects. Combining may cause hypoglycemia. Use only under strict medical monitoring.

caution.name: Cinnamon Extract
caution.reason: May lower blood sugar modestly. Monitor glucose closely if combining with metformin to avoid hypoglycemia.

avoid.name: Alcohol-Based Tinctures
avoid.reason: Alcohol increases lactic acidosis risk with metformin. Avoid liquid supplements with alcohol bases.

avoid.name: Bitter Melon
avoid.reason: Strong blood sugar lowering effect. Combined with metformin can cause dangerously low blood sugar levels.

metformin.timing_note: Take B12 and folate at least 2 hours apart from metformin for optimal absorption. Take metformin with meals.

statin.name: Statins (Cholesterol)

safe.name: CoQ10
safe.reason: Statins block the mevalonate pathway, depleting CoQ10 by up to 40%. Supplementing reduces statin-related muscle pain and supports heart energy production.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Statin users have lower vitamin D levels. Supplementing supports bone health, immune function, and may reduce statin myalgia.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Complements statin therapy by lowering triglycerides. EPA/DHA combined with statins provides superior cardiovascular protection.

safe.name: Vitamin K2
safe.reason: Directs calcium away from arteries and into bones. Statins may impair vitamin K2 metabolism; supplementing supports arterial and bone health.

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: Supports cardiovascular function and may reduce statin-related muscle cramps. Does not interfere with statin metabolism.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: Certain strains help metabolize cholesterol. Supports gut health which can be affected by long-term statin use.

caution.name: Niacin (Vitamin B3)
caution.reason: Low-dose niacin is generally safe, but high-dose niacin (>500 mg) combined with statins increases risk of liver damage and myopathy.

caution.name: Vitamin A
caution.reason: Both statins and high-dose vitamin A are processed by the liver. Combined use may increase hepatotoxicity risk. Keep within RDA.

caution.name: Citrus Bergamot
caution.reason: Has statin-like cholesterol lowering properties. May amplify statin effects; discuss dosing with your doctor.

avoid.name: Red Yeast Rice
avoid.reason: Contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin. Combining with a prescribed statin doubles the dose and dramatically increases muscle damage and liver toxicity risk.

avoid.name: Grapefruit Extract
avoid.reason: Inhibits CYP3A4 liver enzyme that metabolizes most statins. Raises statin blood levels to dangerous concentrations, increasing rhabdomyolysis risk.

avoid.name: St. John's Wort
avoid.reason: Induces CYP3A4 enzymes, dramatically reducing statin blood levels and making the medication ineffective at controlling cholesterol.

statin.timing_note: Take CoQ10 with a fat-containing meal for absorption. If taking a statin at night, take CoQ10 earlier in the day.

ppi.name: PPIs (Acid Reflux)

safe.name: Vitamin B12
safe.reason: PPIs reduce stomach acid needed for B12 absorption. Long-term PPI users have up to 65% higher B12 deficiency risk. Use sublingual or methylcobalamin forms.

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: PPIs cause magnesium depletion in 10-15% of long-term users. Low magnesium causes muscle cramps, arrhythmia, and fatigue. Use glycinate or citrate forms.

safe.name: Calcium
safe.reason: PPIs impair calcium absorption by reducing stomach acid. Use calcium citrate (not carbonate) as it does not require acid for absorption.

safe.name: Iron
safe.reason: Stomach acid is essential for iron absorption. PPI users should use iron bisglycinate, which absorbs independently of stomach pH.

safe.name: Vitamin C
safe.reason: PPIs reduce vitamin C levels in gastric juice. Supplementing supports iron absorption and immune function.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: PPIs alter gut microbiome composition. Probiotics help maintain beneficial bacteria and reduce risk of C. difficile infection associated with PPI use.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: PPI-related calcium malabsorption affects bone density. Vitamin D3 enhances calcium absorption and protects bone health.

safe.name: Zinc
safe.reason: PPIs impair zinc absorption. Zinc carnosine is particularly beneficial as it also supports stomach lining integrity.

caution.name: Digestive Enzymes
caution.reason: May help compensate for reduced acid, but could partially counteract PPI effectiveness. Discuss timing with your doctor.

caution.name: Apple Cider Vinegar
caution.reason: Increases stomach acidity, which opposes PPI action. May be counterproductive if your PPI is prescribed for GERD.

avoid.name: Betaine HCl
avoid.reason: Directly increases stomach acid, completely counteracting the mechanism of PPIs. Do not combine.

avoid.name: High-Dose Mineral Blends
avoid.reason: PPIs already impair mineral absorption. Mega-dose minerals may cause GI distress and compete for limited absorption pathways. Use targeted single minerals instead.

ppi.timing_note: Take ALL supplements at least 2 hours after your PPI dose. Use sublingual B12 and chelated mineral forms for better absorption.

blood-pressure.name: Blood Pressure Medications

safe.name: CoQ10
safe.reason: Many BP medications deplete CoQ10. Meta-analyses show CoQ10 can reduce systolic BP by 11 mmHg, complementing medication therapy.

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: Supports vascular relaxation and may lower BP by 5-6 mmHg. Works synergistically with most blood pressure medications.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Lowers triglycerides and provides modest BP reduction. Safe with all classes of antihypertensives and supports overall cardiovascular health.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Low vitamin D is associated with hypertension. Supplementing supports the renin-angiotensin system and vascular health.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: Emerging research shows certain probiotic strains can modestly lower blood pressure. Safe alongside BP medications.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: Supports homocysteine metabolism and cardiovascular health. Diuretic BP medications may deplete B vitamins.

caution.name: Potassium
caution.reason: ACE inhibitors and ARBs raise potassium levels. Additional potassium supplementation can cause dangerous hyperkalemia. Only use under medical monitoring.

caution.name: Hawthorn Berry
caution.reason: Has vasodilating properties that may enhance BP medication effects. Can cause hypotension. Use only under supervision.

caution.name: Garlic Supplements
caution.reason: Has mild blood pressure lowering effects. Generally safe at standard doses but may add to hypotension risk with aggressive BP treatment.

avoid.name: Licorice Root
avoid.reason: Contains glycyrrhizin, which causes sodium retention and potassium loss, directly counteracting blood pressure medications and raising BP.

avoid.name: Ephedra/Ma Huang
avoid.reason: A potent vasoconstrictor and stimulant that raises blood pressure. Directly opposes antihypertensive therapy and can cause hypertensive crisis.

avoid.name: Yohimbe
avoid.reason: Raises norepinephrine levels and blood pressure. Combining with BP medications can cause dangerous blood pressure fluctuations.

blood-pressure.timing_note: Take magnesium in the evening; it may enhance the nighttime BP-lowering effect. Monitor BP regularly when adding supplements.

birth-control.name: Birth Control Pills

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: Oral contraceptives deplete B6, B12, and folate. Methylated B-complex restores levels and supports mood, energy, and fertility preparation.

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: Birth control depletes magnesium, contributing to headaches, cramps, and mood changes. Supplementing alleviates these common side effects.

safe.name: Zinc
safe.reason: Hormonal contraceptives lower zinc levels by up to 30%. Zinc supports immune function, skin health, and hormone balance.

safe.name: Vitamin C
safe.reason: Oral contraceptives lower vitamin C plasma levels. Supplementing supports immune function and iron absorption.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Supports cardiovascular health (important since birth control slightly increases clot risk) and helps with mood regulation.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: May be affected by hormonal contraceptives. Supports bone health, immune function, and mood.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: Oral contraceptives can affect gut microbiome. Probiotics support digestion, immune health, and nutrient absorption.

caution.name: DIM (Diindolylmethane)
caution.reason: Affects estrogen metabolism. May theoretically alter how the body processes synthetic hormones in birth control. Discuss with your doctor.

caution.name: Vitex (Chasteberry)
caution.reason: Acts on the pituitary gland to affect hormone levels. May interfere with the hormonal mechanism of oral contraceptives.

avoid.name: St. John's Wort
avoid.reason: Induces CYP3A4 liver enzymes that break down contraceptive hormones. Reduces birth control effectiveness and can cause breakthrough bleeding or unintended pregnancy.

avoid.name: Activated Charcoal
avoid.reason: Binds to substances in the gut including contraceptive hormones. Taking within 2-3 hours of birth control can reduce absorption and contraceptive effectiveness.

birth-control.timing_note: Take supplements with meals. Avoid activated charcoal within 3 hours of birth control pill.

thyroid.name: Thyroid Medications

safe.name: Selenium
safe.reason: Essential for thyroid hormone conversion (T4 to T3). Selenium supplementation reduces thyroid antibodies in Hashimoto's patients by up to 40%.

safe.name: Zinc
safe.reason: Required for TSH production and T3 hormone synthesis. Supports overall thyroid function without interfering with medication absorption.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Thyroid patients (especially Hashimoto's) have high rates of vitamin D deficiency. Supplementing supports immune regulation and bone health.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: Supports energy production which is often impaired in hypothyroidism. B12 deficiency is common in autoimmune thyroid disease.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Reduces inflammation associated with autoimmune thyroid conditions. Supports brain function often impaired in hypothyroidism.

caution.name: Iodine
caution.reason: Essential for thyroid hormone production, but excess iodine can worsen Hashimoto's. Only supplement if testing confirms deficiency. Discuss with endocrinologist.

caution.name: Ashwagandha
caution.reason: May stimulate thyroid hormone production. Could cause hyperthyroidism in patients already on thyroid medication. Use only under supervision.

avoid.name: Calcium (within 4 hours)
avoid.reason: Calcium directly binds to thyroid medication in the gut, reducing absorption by up to 60%. Must be taken at least 4 hours apart.

avoid.name: Iron (within 4 hours)
avoid.reason: Iron chelates thyroid hormones in the GI tract, dramatically reducing medication effectiveness. Separate by at least 4 hours.

avoid.name: Magnesium (within 4 hours)
avoid.reason: Magnesium interferes with thyroid medication absorption. Beneficial to take, but MUST be separated by at least 4 hours from your thyroid dose.

thyroid.timing_note: CRITICAL: Take thyroid medication on an empty stomach, 30-60 minutes before food. Wait at least 4 hours before taking any mineral supplements.

warfarin.name: Warfarin (Blood Thinner)

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Does not affect blood clotting. Supports bone health, which is important since long-term warfarin use can reduce bone density.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: Generally safe with warfarin. Supports gut health and does not significantly affect INR levels at standard doses.

safe.name: Vitamin C
safe.reason: Safe at moderate doses (up to 500 mg). Supports immune function without significantly affecting warfarin metabolism or INR.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: Safe with warfarin and supports homocysteine metabolism. Does not affect clotting factors or INR levels.

caution.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
caution.reason: Has mild antiplatelet effects. Low doses (1-2 g) are generally safe but high doses may increase bleeding risk. Monitor INR closely.

caution.name: Magnesium
caution.reason: Generally safe but can affect medication absorption if taken simultaneously. Separate by 2 hours and inform your anticoagulation clinic.

caution.name: CoQ10
caution.reason: Structurally similar to vitamin K and may reduce warfarin's effectiveness in some individuals. Requires INR monitoring if started.

avoid.name: Vitamin K Supplements
avoid.reason: Vitamin K directly counteracts warfarin by activating clotting factors. Even small changes in vitamin K intake can destabilize INR and cause dangerous clots.

avoid.name: Garlic Supplements
avoid.reason: Inhibits platelet aggregation and enhances warfarin's blood-thinning effect. Increases serious bleeding risk including internal hemorrhage.

avoid.name: Ginkgo Biloba
avoid.reason: Potent antiplatelet effects that compound warfarin's anticoagulation. Associated with case reports of serious bleeding events.

avoid.name: High-Dose Ginger
avoid.reason: Inhibits thromboxane synthesis at high doses, enhancing anticoagulation. Increases risk of bleeding complications with warfarin.

warfarin.timing_note: CONSULT YOUR DOCTOR before taking ANY new supplement. Maintain consistent vitamin K dietary intake. Have INR checked after any supplement changes.

antibiotics.name: Antibiotics

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: Antibiotics kill beneficial gut bacteria causing diarrhea in up to 30% of patients. Saccharomyces boulardii and Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG reduce antibiotic-associated diarrhea by 50%.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: Antibiotics disrupt gut bacteria that produce B vitamins (especially K and biotin). Supplementing prevents secondary deficiency.

safe.name: Vitamin C
safe.reason: Supports immune function during infection. Does not interfere with most antibiotic mechanisms and aids recovery.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Supports immune response during active infection. Adequate vitamin D levels improve antibiotic treatment outcomes.

safe.name: Vitamin K
safe.reason: Antibiotics destroy vitamin K-producing gut bacteria. Supplementing prevents deficiency-related bleeding risk, especially with prolonged courses.

caution.name: Zinc
caution.reason: Supports immune function but can bind to fluoroquinolone and tetracycline antibiotics, reducing their absorption. Take 2-4 hours apart.

caution.name: Iron
caution.reason: Chelates with fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines, and penicillins in the gut, reducing antibiotic absorption by up to 75%. Must separate by 2-4 hours.

avoid.name: Calcium (with fluoroquinolones)
avoid.reason: Calcium directly binds to ciprofloxacin and levofloxacin, reducing absorption below therapeutic levels. Separate by at least 2 hours or antibiotic may be ineffective.

avoid.name: Magnesium (with fluoroquinolones)
avoid.reason: Magnesium chelates fluoroquinolone antibiotics, rendering them inactive. If on ciprofloxacin or similar drugs, separate all minerals by 2-4 hours.

antibiotics.timing_note: Take probiotics at least 2 hours away from antibiotic doses. Continue probiotics for at least 7-14 days after finishing the antibiotic course.

nsaid.name: NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen)

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Provides natural anti-inflammatory effects that complement NSAIDs. May allow lower NSAID doses, reducing GI side effects.

safe.name: Curcumin (Turmeric)
safe.reason: Potent natural anti-inflammatory that works via COX-2 and NF-kB pathways. Studies show comparable pain relief to ibuprofen for osteoarthritis.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: NSAIDs damage the gut lining and disrupt microbiome. Probiotics help protect gastric mucosa and reduce GI side effects.

safe.name: Vitamin C
safe.reason: NSAIDs deplete vitamin C and can cause gastric bleeding. Vitamin C supports gut lining integrity and iron absorption.

safe.name: Folate
safe.reason: Long-term NSAID use can impair folate metabolism. Supplementing supports cell repair and cardiovascular health.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Supports bone health and has anti-inflammatory properties. Especially important if using NSAIDs for joint conditions.

caution.name: Iron
caution.reason: NSAIDs cause microscopic GI bleeding, increasing iron loss. Iron supplementation may be needed but can worsen GI irritation. Use gentle forms like bisglycinate.

caution.name: Ginger
caution.reason: Has anti-inflammatory and mild antiplatelet effects. May increase bleeding risk when combined with NSAIDs, especially at high doses.

caution.name: White Willow Bark
caution.reason: Contains salicin, a natural aspirin-like compound. Combining with NSAIDs stacks anti-inflammatory effects and increases GI bleeding risk.

avoid.name: Aspirin or Other NSAIDs
avoid.reason: Stacking NSAIDs dramatically increases gastric ulcer, GI bleeding, and kidney damage risk. Never combine multiple NSAIDs.

avoid.name: High-Dose Vitamin E
avoid.reason: Vitamin E above 400 IU has antiplatelet effects. Combined with NSAIDs, significantly increases risk of bleeding complications.

nsaid.timing_note: Take NSAIDs with food to protect the stomach. Omega-3 and curcumin taken regularly may reduce NSAID dependence over time.

steroids.name: Steroids (Prednisone, etc.)

safe.name: Calcium
safe.reason: Corticosteroids cause bone loss by impairing calcium absorption and increasing excretion. Calcium citrate supplementation is essential for bone protection.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Steroids impair vitamin D metabolism and calcium absorption. D3 supplementation (2000-4000 IU) is critical to prevent steroid-induced osteoporosis.

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: Steroids increase urinary magnesium excretion. Supplementing prevents muscle cramps, insomnia, and cardiovascular issues.

safe.name: Zinc
safe.reason: Corticosteroids deplete zinc and suppress immune function. Zinc supplementation supports immune health and wound healing during steroid therapy.

safe.name: Vitamin C
safe.reason: Steroids increase oxidative stress and impair wound healing. Vitamin C supports collagen synthesis and immune function.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: Steroids suppress immune function and alter gut flora. Probiotics help maintain microbiome diversity and reduce infection risk.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: Steroids can affect B vitamin metabolism. B-complex supports energy production and nervous system function during steroid therapy.

caution.name: Potassium
caution.reason: Steroids cause potassium loss, but supplementation should be guided by blood testing. Excess potassium can cause cardiac arrhythmias.

caution.name: Melatonin
caution.reason: Steroids often cause insomnia. Melatonin can help but may interact with steroid-related immune suppression. Discuss with your doctor.

caution.name: DHEA
caution.reason: Steroids suppress adrenal DHEA production. Replacement may be beneficial but requires hormonal monitoring and medical supervision.

avoid.name: High-Dose Vitamin A
avoid.reason: Both steroids and high-dose vitamin A affect bone metabolism. Combined use may accelerate bone loss and increase osteoporosis risk.

avoid.name: Echinacea
avoid.reason: Stimulates immune function, which directly opposes the immunosuppressive purpose of corticosteroid therapy.

steroids.timing_note: Long-term steroid use requires bone density monitoring. Start calcium + D3 supplementation immediately when beginning steroid therapy.

levothyroxine.name: Levothyroxine (Hypothyroidism)

safe.name: Selenium
safe.reason: Essential cofactor for deiodinase enzymes that convert T4 (levothyroxine) to active T3. Supplementation improves thyroid hormone conversion and reduces autoimmune thyroid inflammation.

safe.name: Zinc
safe.reason: Supports TSH production and thyroid hormone receptor binding. Safe to take with levothyroxine when properly timed (4+ hours apart).

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Hypothyroid patients have significantly higher rates of vitamin D deficiency. Supplementing supports immune regulation and bone health.

safe.name: Vitamin B12
safe.reason: Autoimmune thyroid disease is commonly associated with B12 deficiency. Sublingual B12 does not interfere with levothyroxine absorption.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Reduces inflammation in autoimmune thyroiditis. Supports cardiovascular health, which can be compromised in hypothyroidism.

caution.name: Iodine
caution.reason: Needed for thyroid hormone production, but excessive iodine worsens Hashimoto's disease. Only supplement after testing confirms deficiency.

caution.name: Ashwagandha
caution.reason: May stimulate thyroid function and increase T4 levels. Combined with levothyroxine, could cause hyperthyroid symptoms. Requires dose monitoring.

caution.name: L-Tyrosine
caution.reason: Thyroid hormone precursor. May increase thyroid hormone production beyond what levothyroxine provides. Use only under medical supervision.

avoid.name: Calcium (within 4 hours)
avoid.reason: Calcium forms insoluble complexes with levothyroxine in the GI tract, reducing absorption by up to 60%. Must be separated by at least 4 hours.

avoid.name: Iron (within 4 hours)
avoid.reason: Iron chelates levothyroxine, reducing its bioavailability by up to 75%. Always take iron at least 4 hours after levothyroxine.

avoid.name: Magnesium (within 4 hours)
avoid.reason: Magnesium hydroxide and citrate form insoluble complexes with levothyroxine. Must be separated by at least 4 hours for proper absorption.

avoid.name: Soy Isoflavones
avoid.reason: Soy inhibits thyroid peroxidase and may reduce levothyroxine absorption. Avoid concentrated soy supplements; separate soy foods by 4 hours.

levothyroxine.timing_note: CRITICAL: Take levothyroxine first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with water only. Wait 30-60 minutes before eating. Wait 4+ hours before taking ANY mineral supplement.

adderall.name: Adderall (ADHD)

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: Adderall depletes magnesium and causes muscle tension, jaw clenching, and insomnia. Magnesium glycinate restores levels and reduces stimulant side effects.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Supports brain function and attention. Meta-analyses show omega-3 supplementation improves ADHD symptoms independently and may enhance stimulant medication effects.

safe.name: L-Theanine
safe.reason: Promotes calm focus by increasing alpha brain waves. Smooths out the stimulant curve without sedation, reducing Adderall-related anxiety and jitteriness.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: Amphetamines increase B vitamin utilization for neurotransmitter synthesis. Supplementing prevents depletion and supports dopamine and norepinephrine production.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: ADHD populations often have lower vitamin D levels. Supplementing supports cognitive function and mood regulation.

safe.name: Zinc
safe.reason: Zinc is a cofactor in dopamine synthesis and regulation. Studies show zinc supplementation may improve ADHD symptoms and reduce required stimulant doses.

caution.name: Vitamin C (timing matters)
caution.reason: Vitamin C acidifies urine and increases Adderall excretion, reducing its effectiveness. Take vitamin C in the evening, well after Adderall has been absorbed.

caution.name: Melatonin
caution.reason: Can help with Adderall-related insomnia. Generally safe at low doses (0.5-3 mg) but start low as stimulants may alter melatonin sensitivity.

caution.name: Iron
caution.reason: Low ferritin is linked to worse ADHD symptoms. Test levels before supplementing; excess iron is harmful. Target ferritin above 30 ng/mL.

avoid.name: Caffeine Supplements
avoid.reason: Stacks stimulant effects with Adderall, increasing heart rate, blood pressure, anxiety, and risk of cardiac events. Avoid concentrated caffeine supplements.

avoid.name: Ginseng
avoid.reason: Has stimulant properties that compound Adderall's effects on the cardiovascular system. Increases risk of hypertension and tachycardia.

avoid.name: Yohimbe
avoid.reason: A potent stimulant that raises norepinephrine levels. Combined with Adderall, significantly increases cardiovascular strain and anxiety.

adderall.timing_note: Take supplements 2+ hours away from Adderall. Take vitamin C in the evening only. Magnesium at bedtime helps with sleep.

benzodiazepine.name: Benzodiazepines (Xanax, Valium, Klonopin)

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: Supports nervous system function and may ease anxiety through GABA receptor modulation. Safe at standard doses and does not dangerously amplify benzodiazepine sedation.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: B vitamins support nervous system health and neurotransmitter production. B6 is particularly important for GABA synthesis.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Reduces neuroinflammation and supports brain health. Does not interact with benzodiazepine metabolism and may help with underlying anxiety.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Low vitamin D is associated with increased anxiety. Supplementing supports mood regulation without sedative interaction.

safe.name: Probiotics
safe.reason: The gut-brain axis influences anxiety levels. Specific probiotic strains (L. rhamnosus, B. longum) may help reduce anxiety without pharmacological sedation.

caution.name: L-Theanine
caution.reason: Promotes relaxation and enhances GABA. At standard doses (100-200 mg) likely safe, but may increase sedation. Start with low doses and monitor.

caution.name: Melatonin
caution.reason: Benzodiazepines suppress natural melatonin production. Low-dose melatonin (0.5-1 mg) may help, but higher doses can increase sedation. Consult your doctor.

caution.name: CBD
caution.reason: CBD inhibits CYP3A4, the enzyme that metabolizes most benzodiazepines. This can raise benzo blood levels and increase sedation and respiratory depression risk.

avoid.name: Kava
avoid.reason: A potent GABA agonist that dramatically compounds benzodiazepine sedation. Combining can cause dangerous respiratory depression, extreme sedation, and liver toxicity.

avoid.name: Valerian Root
avoid.reason: Acts on GABA receptors similarly to benzodiazepines. Combined use causes excessive CNS depression, impaired coordination, and respiratory risk.

avoid.name: GABA Supplements
avoid.reason: Directly targets the same receptor system as benzodiazepines. Stacking compounds sedation and increases risk of dangerous CNS depression.

avoid.name: Phenibut
avoid.reason: A synthetic GABA analog with potent sedative effects. Combining with benzodiazepines is extremely dangerous and can cause coma or respiratory failure.

benzodiazepine.timing_note: Do NOT combine with any sedating supplements. If you currently take sedating supplements and are starting a benzodiazepine, inform your doctor immediately.

beta-blocker.name: Beta-Blockers (Metoprolol, Atenolol, Propranolol)

safe.name: CoQ10
safe.reason: Beta-blockers inhibit CoQ10-dependent enzymes, depleting levels by up to 40%. Supplementing reduces fatigue, muscle weakness, and supports heart energy production.

safe.name: Melatonin
safe.reason: Beta-blockers suppress melatonin secretion by blocking pineal beta-1 receptors. Supplementing with 0.5-3 mg restores sleep quality disrupted by beta-blockers.

safe.name: Magnesium
safe.reason: Supports cardiovascular function and may help with beta-blocker side effects like fatigue. Works synergistically for heart rhythm regulation.

safe.name: Vitamin D3
safe.reason: Supports cardiovascular and bone health. Does not interfere with beta-blocker metabolism and addresses common deficiency in cardiac patients.

safe.name: Omega-3 Fish Oil
safe.reason: Provides additional cardiovascular protection alongside beta-blockers. May help with triglyceride levels and inflammatory markers.

safe.name: B-Complex
safe.reason: Supports energy production which is often reduced as a side effect of beta-blockers. Helps maintain homocysteine levels for cardiovascular health.

caution.name: Potassium
caution.reason: Some beta-blockers (non-selective types) can increase potassium levels. Supplementing without blood testing can cause dangerous hyperkalemia.

caution.name: Hawthorn Berry
caution.reason: Has cardiac effects that may enhance beta-blocker action. Could cause excessive heart rate reduction (bradycardia). Use only under medical supervision.

caution.name: Garlic Supplements
caution.reason: May enhance blood pressure lowering effects. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension like dizziness when combining.

avoid.name: High-Dose Calcium
avoid.reason: Excessive calcium can interfere with cardiac electrical conduction. Combined with beta-blockers, may cause severe bradycardia or heart block.

avoid.name: Ephedra/Ma Huang
avoid.reason: A strong stimulant that directly opposes beta-blocker therapy. Can cause dangerous blood pressure spikes and rebound tachycardia.

avoid.name: Bitter Orange (Synephrine)
avoid.reason: Contains sympathomimetic compounds that counteract beta-blockade. May cause hypertensive crisis when combined with beta-blockers.

beta-blocker.timing_note: Take CoQ10 with meals for absorption. Melatonin at bedtime to restore sleep disrupted by beta-blockers.
